findings.text: Allocator that first obtains a candidate address from the generic unmapped-area provider and then optionally improves alignment for large-page use. It declines improvement when huge support is unavailable, when configuration denies huge use, when the caller pins the address, when a caller hint is already satisfied, or when length is smaller than the large-page unit. Otherwise it reserves a larger span and shifts the result so file offset and virtual address agree modulo large-page size, falling back to the original candidate on any failure.

Locking helper for shared-memory files that tracks a persistent locked flag. Transition from unlocked to locked charges the whole file size against the caller allowance and marks the mapping unevictable; transition back uncharges and clears the mark when accounting context is supplied. Repeated requests in the same state succeed without additional charging.

Fault entry for shared-memory mappings. It first honors coordination with concurrent hole removal and otherwise obtains a cached folio for the faulting index, publishes the corresponding page to the caller and reports the locked state. Acquisition errors are translated to fault error results.

Coordination between fault path and hole-punch path uses a per-inode publication slot. When a punch is published and the fault index lies inside the published interval, the fault sleeps uninterruptibly until the puncher clears the publication and wakes waiters, then requests a retry if it released mapping protection for sleeping. Faults outside the interval proceed without waiting.

Inode spin protection guards the private coordination pointer and its associated wait-queue pointer. Both fault-side waiting and punch-side publication and wakeup hold this protection while installing, inspecting, or clearing the publication, with sleep occurring only after release and re-acquisition before completing the wait.

Exclusive inode ownership serializes fallocate, write iteration, and data-or-hole seeking against size and range mutation. Write preparation assumes the caller already holds this ownership. Read and splice paths operate without it and therefore revalidate size after folio lookup.

Large-page alignment preference favors shared mappings and also private mappings until copy-on-write, but always respects a successful caller address hint. Anonymous requests without a file derive a suitable alignment unit from the highest enabled small-huge order when the filesystem does not forbid huge use; otherwise the default large-page unit applies.

Memory-policy handling delegates shared policy storage to the inode-specific policy object. Lookup biases interleaving by inode number and resolves by linear page index within the area, leaving order-dependent offset adjustment to the caller.

Mapping preparation records file access and chooses mapping operations based on link presence: linked files use the shared-memory operations while unlinked files use the anonymous variant, reflecting anonymous shared memory when unlinked at map time.
Open handling enables direct-input capability on the file mode and then delegates to the generic file open behavior.
Extended-attribute initialization for this file type is absent; the corresponding hook is defined as null.

Userfault handling for shared memory is exposed as a table of five callbacks covering permission check, non-allocating lookup, fresh allocation, cache insertion, and cache removal. The permission check unconditionally allows handling, and lookup uses a non-allocating folio query that propagates errors as pointer-encoded failures.

Fresh allocation for userfault fill refuses indexes at or beyond end of file as derived from rounded-up size, allocates an order-zero folio with mapping-derived allocation flags, and abandons the folio when group charging fails.

Insertion of a freshly filled folio marks it locked and swap-backed, adds it to the page cache, accounts one block with rollback to cache removal on accounting failure, then places it on reclaim tracking and refreshes inode statistics. Removal undoes cache presence and statistics and releases the lock.
Two inode-operation tables for symbolic-link handling are declared but not defined in these fragments.

Write preparation rejects growth, content mutation, or future-write extensions forbidden by seal state, and rejects growth beyond current size when the mapping is marked frozen. It then acquires a writable folio for the starting index and fails the operation when the folio contains poisoned storage.

Write completion extends file size when the written span passes end of file, initializes unwritten portions of a previously non-current folio by clearing head and tail gaps before marking it current, then marks dirty and releases lock and reference, reporting the copied length.

Sequential read iterates over the requested span, looking up each index without allocating on absence, revalidating size after lookup to cope with concurrent truncation, flushing cache coherence when the mapping is writably mapped, marking accessed on aligned starts, and sourcing holes from a shared zero source rather than storage.

Write iteration serializes the whole operation under exclusive inode ownership and applies generic size validation, privilege stripping, timestamp update, and generic write execution in that contracted order.

Piping of zero-filled ranges uses a dedicated pipe-buffer operations table whose acquire always succeeds, whose release is a no-op, and whose steal attempt always declines, ensuring the shared zero page is never captured by the pipe.

Splice from file to pipe limits total length by remaining pipe capacity, resolves each position to either a cached folio or a hole, handles poison by failing, flushes coherence when writably mapped, and splices folio-backed ranges through the folio path and holes through a zero-page pipe entry bounded by page remainder, updating position and readahead state until length exhausts or pipe fills.

Seeking delegates all modes other than data and hole location to the generic sized seek. Data and hole location validate non-negative origin under exclusive inode ownership, query the mapping for next data or hole bounded by current size, and install the result as the new file position when found.

Hole removal validates mode and frozen or sealed state under exclusive ownership, publishes a stack-resident wait queue with page-aligned start and end to coordinate concurrent faults, unmaps fully covered pages from mappings, discards the byte range from storage, then clears the publication, wakes all waiters, and asserts no waiter remains.

Non-punch allocation rejects unsupported mode bits, checks frozen state, validates size limits and growth seals, guards against arithmetic overflow when page-aligning the end, and preemptively fails when the requested page span exceeds the filesystem block budget.

Coordination record carries a wait-queue pointer plus start and next page indexes delimiting the coordinated interval, with additional counters for allocation versus unswapped progress in the allocation path.

Poisoned storage is treated as input-output failure across write preparation, read, and splice paths. Large folios containing poisoned subpages fall back from whole-folio copy or splice to single-page handling in read and splice paths.

The punch wait queue resides on the punching task stack, so fault-side waiters may hold a pointer that becomes invalid after wakeup. Correctness relies on completion handling that avoids dereferencing the queue in that case while still serializing against concurrent wakeup with inode spin protection.

Huge-alignment improvement must never fail the mapping; every exceptional condition including oversize inflated reservation, arithmetic wrap, allocation failure, misalignment, or result beyond address limit falls back to the originally obtained address.

Observed selectors include FALLOC_FL_KEEP_SIZE and FALLOC_FL_PUNCH_HOLE for allocation modes, F_SEAL_GROW and F_SEAL_WRITE and F_SEAL_FUTURE_WRITE for seals, SHMEM_F_LOCKED and SHMEM_F_MAPPING_FROZEN for inode state, MAP_FIXED for mapping requests, FMODE_CAN_ODIRECT for open mode, TASK_UNINTERRUPTIBLE for wait state, SEEK_DATA and SEEK_HOLE for seek modes.

Fault and status reporting observed uses VM_FAULT_NOPAGE and VM_FAULT_RETRY and VM_FAULT_LOCKED for fault outcomes, SGP_CACHE and SGP_READ and SGP_WRITE and SGP_NOALLOC and SGP_FALLOC for folio acquisition modes, and ENOMEM EPERM EOPNOTSUPP EFBIG EINTR ENXIO EIO EFAULT EINVAL ENOSPC for failure reporting.
